ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl: Let m = floor(nr). By the definition of the floor function, m is an integer satisfying m <= nr < m + 1. Since n > 1, we have n > 0, so dividing the inequality by the positive number n preserves the inequality signs. Therefore m/n <= r < (m + 1)/n. This is exactly the desired statement.
payload.role_in_assembly: Places r inside the same normalized interval as m/n.
